description:
We are very interested in developing software for farmers; 
The farm and the field serve as a testing ground for implementing all kinds of modern technologies and ideas.
summary:
Rivnova is an SI-powered precision agriculture platform that turns NASA satellite data into clear, ready-to-use decisions for farmers. Instead of showing raw charts, Rivnova analyzes soil moisture, rainfall, vegetation health, and plant stress signals for each individual field, and tells farmers exactly what to do and when.
Farmers get smart irrigation recommendations, 48-hour safe windows for spraying and field work, early warnings about hidden crop stress before it becomes visible, alerts about unusual vegetation changes, and a 7-day outlook of soil stress. Everything is organized in a prioritized alert center, so the most urgent actions come first. The platform keeps working even when live data sources are temporarily unavailable.
This matters because farmers can save water, avoid preventable yield losses, and react to risks days earlier. Rivnova makes NASA Earth observation data practical for everyday farming, improving both profitability and sustainability.
details:
Rivnova is a smart agriculture platform that helps farmers make better day-to-day decisions for each field. The system combines field geometry (maps), weather and climate context, and agronomic logic to generate practical insights like irrigation timing, crop-condition trends, and risk-aware planning support. The core benefit is turning raw environmental data into clear, actionable recommendations, so teams can improve yield consistency, reduce waste, and react faster to changing conditions.

The intended impact is to make precision agriculture more accessible: not only for large operations with expensive tooling, but also for smaller farms that need reliable, data-driven guidance. We designed the project to support both realistic live workflows and demo scenarios, so it can be validated, presented, and iterated quickly while still reflecting real production constraints (performance, resilience, and data quality).

Technically, we built Rivnova using .NET 10 / C# (ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs), PostgreSQL + PostGIS for geospatial field data, EF Core, and NetTopologySuite/GeoJSON for spatial processing. For frontend React, TypeScript, Vite, TailwindCSS, React Router, TanStack Query, React Leaflet, Leaflet, Leaflet-Geoman, Recharts, FontAwesome. For SI/ML, models are trained in Python (scikit-learn and PyTorch) and exported to ONNX, then executed in production with ONNX Runtime directly in the .NET backend.
Rivnova uses two models for different tasks:
• Yield — Random Forest (train_yield_model.py): The inputs are a small set of seasonal features, and yield depends on nonlinear interactions between them. Random Forest is a practical choice for tabular data: it handles nonlinear relationships without feature scaling and is less sensitive to outliers than a single decision tree. KNN relies on meaningful distances between scaled features, which is awkward here—especially with crop type represented as a number—and can perform poorly with limited or unevenly distributed data.
• Soil forecast — 1D-CNN + GRU (train_soil_forecast.py): This task uses 14 days of ordered weather and soil observations to predict the next 7 days. The CNN can learn short-term patterns, while the GRU models how those patterns evolve over time.

Both models are trained offline and exported to ONNX for inference inside the .NET API.
